newsitem.title: UK: St Paul sees scope in alternative funding.
newsitem.headline: St Paul sees scope in alternative funding.

text.p: A good start for George Town Re has prompted St. Paul Cos Inc to consider similar methods of attracting new capital to expand its insurance business in the future.
"We believe a shift in the business is going to happen and it is important to be at the leading edge." Mike Wacek, managing director St Paul Re UK, told Reuters on Wednesday.

George Town Re is one of a growing breed of securitised reinsurance transactions. Put together in association with Goldman Sachs, George Town Re has attracted $44.5 million from unit or bondholders and $24 million in three-year unprotected preference shares.
The company was launched in December 1996, and originally aimed to raise $100 million from the capital markets to provide extra capacity for St Paul Re.
St Paul Re has signed a 10 year reinsurance treaty with George Town and will cede certain lines on a proportional lines on a proportional basis. St Paul does not own the facility.

Despite only raising $68.5 million, St Paul said it is pleased with the results so far and expected to repeat the exercise. "We have been able to increase our commitment to some key clients, especially in the U.S. and UK," said Wacek.
"We are very pleased with how George Town Re is serving our needs at this early stage."

In its first six months St Paul Re has used the additional retrocessional capacity to increase its line sizes outside of the U.S., improving its ability to sell more innovative products and increasing its exposure in the catastrophe market.
It is also hoped that increased line size will improve the company's pricing power, although this has not yet materialised, Wacek said.
The George Town Re facility also enables St Paul Re to make better use of its existing staff and systems.
However, Wacek said this alternative method of reinsurance funding would not replace traditional reinsurance.
